NAME: temp
DESCRIPTION: Placeholder region supplied for the ground rig cycle. 48x64 blocks of 16 px, which is 48x64 walk tiles -- this art was already on the tile grid, so the tile law left it unchanged. Well short of the ~155 tiles the tile-exact framing needs; its plane edges are expected to show. Naming this region is a lore question, not decided here.

NAME: temp2
DESCRIPTION: Second placeholder region, supplied 2026-09-01. 31x22 blocks of 8 px, drawn on the CEL grid -- so under the tile law it is 15.5 x 11 walk tiles, not 31x22, and it renders at half the ground it used to cover. Legacy painted art, deliberately not re-cut. Seven colours, no alpha, sea-dominant.

NAME: temp2_authored
DESCRIPTION: The first authored region: composed from tile data rather than painted. Its source is data/worldmap/authored/temp2_authored.json and its TEXTURE is a BUILD ARTIFACT baked from it -- generated, never hand-edited, committed so a fresh checkout renders without running a bake. 15x11 walk tiles, reassembled from tiles cut out of temp2, and the bake reproduces temp2's first 240 px byte for byte. temp2 is 15.5 tiles wide, so its rightmost 8 px is a cel-grade remainder this tile-grade map does not cover.

NAME: temp2_hex32
DESCRIPTION: Flat-top hex prototype region, 32 px hexes reassembled from temp2_hex32_ground. 20 hexes across x 10 rows. A hex is 32 px = 2 world units wide under the current 16 px world unit, so columns advance 1.5 units. Ground only -- the nine structures are painted out and return later as placed objects. Prototype for judging hex framing; GRID 1 because the hex lattice does not land on a square block size.

NAME: hex_battle_fixture
DESCRIPTION: The battle-map fixture authored for HXB-10: temp2_hex32_authored's geometry, art and nine building objects, plus a tactical layer marking which cells a battle is fought on and what each costs to cross. 20 x 10 hexes, of which 95 are playable; the border is deliberately off the board. Flat at elevation 0 throughout -- terrain heights are continuous over the shared hex vertex lattice, so two adjacent PLAYABLE cells cannot differ in elevation without a slope between them, and the tactical export refuses a sloped cell rather than rounding it. Its TEXTURE is a BUILD ARTIFACT baked from the source document; its gameplay scene is exported, not committed. Inherited art, not the target look.
